sentences.text: Dated this the 10th day of January, 2025
COMMONORDER These Bail Applications are filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
2. These bail applications are connected and therefore, I am disposing of these bail applications by a common order.
3. Petitioner in these bail applications are one and the same.
Petitioner is one of the accused in Crime No.18/2022, 29/2022 and 49/2022 of CBCID, Thrissur.
The above case is registered against the petitioner alleging offences interalia under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

The prosecution case is that, petitioner in these cases are the members of the Board of Directors of Karivannur Service Cooperative Bank Ltd Karivannur, in which fraudulent 2025:KER:2566 BAIL APPL. NOS.11004, 11001 & 11011 OF 2024 activities are detected to have been committed, by accused Nos.1 to 6 with dishonest intention to cheat the bank and its depositors deliberately violating the provisions of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act and Rules and committed forgery and mis-appropriated and siphoned off huge amount of the bank.

entities.text: Karivannur Service Cooperative Bank Ltd Karivannur
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Kerala Co-operative Societies Act and Rules
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The main allegation against the petitioner, who is one of the directors of the board is that he in this capacity as the Board director has colluded with the other accused in the alleged offence.

It is the case of the petitioner that, it is upon the complaint filed by him and other board of directors that the illegality committed by the accused Nos.1 to 6 was brought to the notice of the authorities.

4. Heard counsel for the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.
5.
The counsel for the petitioner submitted that, the petitioner is not involved in these cases.
He is falsely implicated in these cases.
Several cases are registered against the petitioner.

This Court granted Anticipatory bail in all those cases as evident by Annexure A4.
2025
. The Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.

4 7.

sentences.text: This Court considered the contention of the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.
After hearing both sides and also considering Annexure A4 order, I think bail can be granted after imposing stringent conditions.
8. Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chidambaram.

P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870],
after considering all the earlier judgments, observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

entities.text: P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Recently the Apex Court in Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
considered the point in detail.

entities.text: Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the above judgment is extracted hereunder.

"12. We may note that personal liberty is an important 2025:KER:2566 BAIL APPL.
NOS.11004, 11001 & 11011 OF 2024 aspect of our constitutional mandate.

The occasion to arrest an accused during investigation arises when custodial investigation becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.
Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.
A distinction must be made between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.
(Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981))

entities.text: Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person.

If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact, throughout cooperated with the investigation we fail to appreciate why there should be a compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused."
10.

In Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961], the Apex Court observed that even if the allegation is one of grave economic offence, it is not a rule that bail should be denied in every case.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the dictum laid down in the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this 2025:KER:2566 BAIL APPL. NOS.11004, 11001 & 11011 OF 2024 case, this Bail Application is allowed with the following directions:
1. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.

2. After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the petitioner, he shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer concerned.

The petitioner shall co-operate with the investigation and shall not,
directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case 2025:KER:2566 BAIL APPL. NOS.11004, 11001 & 11011 OF 2024 so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
4. Petitioner shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.

5. Petitioner shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused,
or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

6. Needless to mention, it would be well within the powers of the investigating officer to investigate the matter and, if necessary, to effect recoveries on the information, if any, given by the petitioner even while the petitioner is on bail as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663].
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

The prosecution and the victim are at liberty to approach the jurisdictional Court to cancel the bail, if any of the above conditions are violated.
